text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning.

- Four out of ten people are still undecided over which party they will vote for in the election in September. A recent opinion poll showed support for ruling Labour Party declining by 1.7 percent during April.

- Employees in both insurer Storebrand and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse want the state to play an active role in the planned merger between the two companies. Based on the state's current shareholding in Christiania, it would own 25 percent of the merged financial giant Christiania. In the revised budget on Tuesday the government said it would consider buying an additional 8.3 percent if the merger goes through.

- Norway's largest shipping company Bergesen posted higher than expected pre-tax profits of 185 million crowns for the first quarter. Bergesen said improved markets in both tankers and gas carriers would lead to higher profits in 1997 than in 1996.

- Construction and engineering group Kvaerner ASA booked a profit of 230 million crowns after selling its stake in British rival Amec Plc. The sale means that Kvaerner has achieved its plan to sell non-core assets of 10 billion crowns one year ahead of schedule.
- Norway's largest natural gas customers are under investigation by the European Union (EU) following accusations of breaking EU competition rules.
